## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded, but it establishes only the stated ideal-generating set, not the direct-sum Schur-basis formula.
- claim-2: The proof is mathematically correct conditional on the displayed box-Schur realization of \(I_{r,q}\). The LR containment argument proves the direct-sum formula for \(J_{p,c}\); the basiswise map kills exactly the classes outside \((i+1)^{j+1}\), retains precisely the basis of \(J_{1,1}\), and therefore restricts surjectively. \(\Lambda\)-linearity then gives the asserted descent. The case \(p=c=1\) is handled. Unconditionally, the certificate remains unestablished because applicability of the box-Schur realization to the source’s \(I_{r,q}\) is not grounded.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Supply an exact source excerpt defining or proving, for the same \(\Lambda\), coefficient ring, and \(I_{r,q}\), that
  \[
  I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda
  \]
  and that the surviving \(\bar s_\lambda\), \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\).

## Required revisions
- Either provide that grounding item or explicitly conclude that the named certificate is established only under the box-Schur realization, not unconditionally.
